measurement: mean retinal ganglion cell density in the main retina, derived as (optic-nerve axons minus axons in the diverticular fascicle) divided by main-retina area
method: axon counts in ultrathin electron-microscope sections taken from random areas covering at least 20% of each structure, extrapolated to the whole structure; divided by retinal area
conditions: Table 2, one fish: D. longipes SL 102 mm, one eye. Axons in optic nerve 14,182; axons in diverticular fascicle 3,487; main retina area 12.60 mm2. The value is an average over the retina, not a peak density, and is not a direct cell count (asterisked row: calculated by subtraction). Specimen chemically fixed (Methods: most eyes fixed in paraformaldehyde and glutaraldehyde; fixative for this fish not stated separately). The diverticular retina of the same eye is 1788 per mm2 (2.1 times denser).
where: Table 2 (header cut and marked; row quoted whole)

measurement: mean retinal ganglion cell density in the diverticular retina (axons in the diverticular fascicle divided by diverticular-retina area)
method: axon counts in ultrathin electron-microscope sections taken from random areas covering at least 20% of each structure, extrapolated to the whole structure; divided by retinal area
conditions: Table 2, one fish: D. longipes SL 102 mm, one eye. Axons in diverticular fascicle 3,487; diverticular retina area 1.95 mm2. Average density, not a peak density. The main retina of the same eye is 849 per mm2 (derived by subtraction). In the other species in the table, R. natalensis, the diverticular retina is less dense than the main retina (47.0 against 76.2 per mm2). Fixed specimen.

measurement: eye diameter as a percentage of standard length, laboratory-reared individual 12 at 370 days
method: horizontal diameter of both eyes measured at 40x magnification on live fish through development
conditions: Cave catfish population kept in the laboratory, offspring of wild-caught adults. Individual 12 was the longest-living fish; in the Results the paper says no perceptible regression in its eye diameter relative to SL occurred up to the 370th day, with fluctuating asymmetry in eye size from the 350th day. The wild-caught adults in the same population have eyes reduced to externally visible spots (Methods fragment: diameters approximately 0.85% of SL in two adults of 64.7 and 63.0 mm SL) or no externally visible eyes, so this value is for a young fish, not the adult condition. One individual; the sentence does not give a left/right split.
